touches.text: Machine: route, the sieves (enabled, never_routed, serves_kind, keyed, addressed) built with the nest machine (16.2), cheapest survivor first. Nests are how the inference proxy resolves its routing questions. The shake ranks instead of cutting for the pick: the survivors stay the set the measure band lets out, a postprocess sieve stamps each one with its rank, and route reads the walk order from those stamps, so the walk still falls over to the next rung. WHY: the walk dials the next rung when a host does not answer, so it needs the whole order, and the compare belongs inside the nest (Akien, 2026-09-29: "i really like option c"). A domain row names the models it may use; the general domain names none, so any model may serve it. The walk goes cheapest first among a domain's models and never leaves them: programming falls from one capable model to the next, never down to a cheaper one outside its set, and when none of its models answers, route refuses, loudly. The set is a sieve in the nest like the others, not a sort after it. WHY: Akien, 2026-11-10, Q#83: "a programming domain will want a specific set of models to be selected from, because we wouldn't replace fable with haiku just to save cash and still be successful." Measured the same day: route.py:301 only reorders a domain's `prefers` to the front, so the walk still falls to cheaper models outside the set.
WHY: the base-most things (the six truths, logging, diagnostics, the core patterns) must be the same everywhere, so they are written once and inherited.
Logging and diagnostics, including diagnostic_inspector: the smart reader of the dumb breadcrumbs base's logging leaves; complete diagnosis on the first pass.
